HOOK
Most people think a massive botnet takedown is a victory. They're wrong.

WHAT
Dutch authorities just dismantled a botnet infecting 17 million devices globally. This disrupted criminal operations temporarily.

WHY IS IT IMPORTANT
The takedown removed one network, but the 17 million infected devices are still out there. Often undetected. Often yours.

WHAT DOES THIS MEAN FOR LEADERS
If your incident response plan doesn't account for large-scale compromise, it's inadequate. If your vendor risk management ignores botnet exposure, your supply chain is vulnerable. This isn't relief. It's a warning.

The botnet takedown impacting 17 million devices isn't a victory. It's a warning shot.

Criminals will shift tactics fast. They'll abandon large botnets for smaller, stealthier networks. Think swarms, not empires.

Tomorrow's threats will be harder to detect. They'll target supply chains with low-footprint malware. Your traditional defenses will be ineffective.

Don't wait for the next takedown. Anticipate the next evolution.
